A fat glow-worm laid in a hollow scooped into the moss pad, its cool gold rising up to warm the underside of each upright grass cord to amber, while a folded dock leaf arched over it keeps the glow from her eyes — one bead has rolled to the very lip of the hollow and stopped there.

A rose-hip with a twisted grass wick set behind the work, its red skin turning all the light ember-orange so the near row of pins glows copper and her knuckle goes rose-gold, one moth asleep on the rim with wings spread flat.

A stub of beeswax in a curl of birch bark propped shield-wise at the far side, throwing only a thin apricot stripe across the wet moss and the backs of her fingers, while a snail makes its slow crossing directly through the warm stripe.

A bead of amber warmed between her palms until it shines from inside, then set down in a crack with a broad sycamore leaf bent over it, gilding the near edge of the stone surface and one cold thumbnail gold.

A candle in a snail shell wedged into a knothole behind her, its aperture aimed at the work alone, laying a warm ivory pool along the row of pebbles on the stone and making the damp limestone go briefly gold.

Three glow-worms folded inside a dock leaf held under her chin, the green-gold seeping up to light the underside of her jaw and the stretched skin between her fingers while her eyes stay free above, a dewdrop on her wrist gone milky-warm.

A little pot of ember-moss with its lid slid half across, set down in a rain-pool hollow so the orange rises upward and stripes the hanging bead-cords from beneath in apricot, a beetle clinging to one cord directly in the warmth.

An ember carried in a walnut shell and blown on gently, the shell cupped in both hands so only the seam glows, that thin red-gold line falling across the moss pad and igniting the brass-pin heads in a row of tiny sparks.

A dish of oil burning one low flame sunk into a hollow in the bark, a curl of cork propped in front so only the overflow light reaches her, turning the nearest grass cords from teal to warm gold at every knot.

A bracket fungus on the trunk just behind her shoulders, glowing honey-warm entirely by itself, edging the full length of her outstretched arm in soft apricot and catching the highest bead on the cord in a bright point of amber.

A handful of luminous seeds cupped in one palm, fingers half-closed, the gaps between them leaking gold across the stone surface and making the row of pebbles cast tiny warm shadows toward her, one seed having rolled between two pebbles and lodged there.

A hollowed rose-hip with a floss wick, set low and behind the work so its red-filtered glow reaches only the near edge of the moss pad and the side of her jaw, a dry grass seed-head catching the ember-orange and going briefly copper.

A firefly in a walnut shell with a sycamore leaf bent over it as a hood, the gold leaking forward in a fan across the upright cords, warming them from silver-green to honeyed amber, a second firefly orbiting the outside of the shell.

A hot river pebble lifted from an earlier fire and wrapped in wet leaves, glowing at every split seam in deep rose-gold, set behind the work so only the seam-light streaks across the moss and the backs of three pinheads.

A curl of resinous pine bark with a grass wick burning in it, propped at a low angle so the flame faces the stone surface and away from her eyes, the pine resin making the light amber-green and the pebble row go gold on one side only.

A glow-worm on a twig laid across a hollow scooped into the bark, a broad petal folded over it, the diffused rose-gold coming up through the petal's veins and landing on her spread fingers and the near knot of grass cord in warm pink.

A bead of amber hung on a thorn and held close to the work, just behind the row of pins, so its inner glow touches each pin-head and the damp moss below them, her thumbnail gone translucent apricot where it rests against the amber.

A clay cup of ember-moss tipped onto its side in a root hollow, its open mouth aimed at the pad, the orange breath of it falling across the threads strung between pins and making each thread a fine line of ember-gold.

A firefly persuaded onto a twig stub wedged in a crack below the working surface, a half-walnut shell set over it as a dome with one edge propped up by a pebble, the escaping gold catching the underside of the moss pad green-gold.

A snail shell with a beeswax stub inside, set far to one side and half behind a root, its opening aimed sideways so only the edge of its ivory light reaches the cord and makes one hanging bead glow turquoise-warm on its near face.

A folded rose petal wrapped around a glow-worm and pinched into a cone, the magenta skin turning the light deep rose-red, held up under the work so the cords above are lit from below in warm crimson while her eyes stay cool above.

A split acorn cap with an ember of moss burning inside, its lid propped half over it by a thorn, the orange gap of it directed at the stone where the pebbles sit, making the wet pebbles shine in a row of amber mirrors.

A luminous seed pod split open and laid in the root fork below the working surface, its cold blue-green turning apricot where the resin inside has dried, the glow reaching the lowest hanging bead and stopping there, one hair-fine grass fibre catching it crosswise.

A wad of ember-moss in a cupped leaf held down at knee height, the leaf folded so only one edge lets the orange out, that stripe of warmth rising to catch the near face of each upright cord and leave the far face in violet cool.

A firefly in a hollowed elder berry, the deep-purple skin filtering the glow to rich rose, set in a crack below the moss pad, the rose light rising through the moss itself so the whole pad glows pink-orange from inside like a hot coal.

A fat glow-worm laid in a hollow scooped from the work-surface, a curl of oak bark tilted over it as a lid, so the glow comes up through the gap and turns the row of upright grass cords amber-gold, one bead swinging.

A hollowed rose-hip with a twist of milkweed floss for a wick, cupped inside her free hand so the red skin diffuses it, washing one cheekbone and the underside of her jaw in deep ember-orange, a moth settled on her wrist untroubled.

A candle-stub of beeswax set inside a snail shell sunk into a crack in the bark behind her, its glow coming forward only in a thin apricot seam that catches the near rim of the moss pad and her knuckles.

Three glow-worms folded into a dock-leaf packet held under her chin, the leaf pressed mostly shut so only the fold-seam leaks gold, lighting the underside of her chin and the fine edges of a folded wing in warm rose-amber.

A bead of warmed amber resting in a nutshell half-lid, slid behind the nearest grass cord, so it throws a honey stripe across two cords and the tips of her outstretched fingers, a dewdrop on the cord gone molten above it.

A dish of oil burning a single low flame, sunk into a rain-pool hollow in the surface, a bent sycamore seed-wing propped at an angle as a baffle so the light rises only on the far side and gilds the row of pebbles gold.

A firefly shut in a walnut shell with a broad plantain leaf bent down over the hinge as a hood, set low on the surface ahead of her so a warm apricot fan falls across the near pins and the edge of the moss.

A stub of beeswax burning in a curl of birch bark propped as a shield, flame on the far side, sending a narrow gold stripe only across the backs of her reaching fingers and one upright twig post, a tiny beetle gripping the twig in the warmth.

A hot river pebble lifted from a distant ember-pile, wrapped in broad leaves that glow tawny at every seam, set behind the whole instrument so only a rim of apricot creeps around to touch her shoulder-blade and the outermost hung bead.

A bracket fungus on the trunk immediately behind her, glowing honey-warm without any flame, edging the full length of her spine and one wing-vein in gold while leaving everything she looks at ahead of her in undisturbed cool teal.

An ember carried inside a split acorn cap, blown on once so it pulses orange, held in her cupped palm at hip height with four fingers clamped over it, the gaps between each finger leaking rose-gold across her knuckles and the nearest grass cord.

A little pot of ember-moss with its fitted bark lid slid a quarter open and turned to face the surface, so a low orange rectangle lights the undersides of a row of hanging beads like lanterns above a street, one bead askew on its cord.

A handful of luminous seeds in a cupped palm, fingers pressed together except at the thumb-gap, leaking a stripe of soft gold that crosses the stone where pebbles are laid and turns the wet moss between them to warm chartreuse.

A firefly inside a hollow acorn cap with a pine-resin plug closing the wide end except for a crescent slot, the slot aimed downward so the gold light falls only on the cords below and leaves her eyes entirely untouched.

A glow-worm on a twig laid across the lip of a bark-bowl so it overhangs the working surface, its cold green-gold tipped warm by the pink of the bowl's inner wood, lighting the pebble row below in apricot while a snail crosses the whole far end.

A rose-hip lamp set inside a folded reed screen with only the stem-end gap facing the work, its red-filtered light coming out as a narrow ember beam across the nearest grass cords and the tips of two pins, the shadow of a grass knot sharp in it.

A stub of beeswax in a clamshell set down in a mossy crevice behind and below the working pad, lid propped to throw the glow upward and forward in one warm wedge that catches the hanging bead-cords from beneath in gold.

A single glow-worm pressed gently under a dome of curved bark held down by a pebble, a notch in the bark's rim aimed at the work, so a thread of rose-lime light crosses the moss surface and picks out one pin's tiny head.

An ember in a nutshell set on a twig stand and tented over with a folded fern pinna, the frond's lacy edge casting a row of tiny amber arcs across the near surface and the outside of her wrist, a rolled-up woodlouse wedged at the stem.

A beeswax stub inside a hollow reed laid sideways, the open end plugged with red rose-petal so all light comes out rose-tinted through the gap at the far end, falling as a warm magenta stripe across the pad of moss and one lifted finger.

Three glow-worms tucked under a dome of lifted shelf-lichen propped on two seed-husks, the gap between them aimed at the work, the pale lime of the worms turned amber by the lichen's own honey tint and landing on the cord-row in warm gold.

A dish of oil sunk into a bark hollow with a half-tile of flat stone slid across most of the top, leaving a finger-width slot on the near side so only a low orange line escapes and paints the underside of the nearest ring of carved wood.

A firefly in a folded birch-bark cone with the point aimed downward at the surface, the wide top pressed shut in her fingers, so the gold seeps only at the cone-tip and makes a small apricot circle on the wet stone below.

A fat glow-worm set in a shallow acorn cap resting on the surface behind her right knee, glowing green-warm with a hint of rose from the cup's tannin stain, putting a rim of soft gold along the outside edge of her ankle and the nearest cord.

A warmed amber bead threaded on a grass cord and swung to rest against the back face of an upright twig post, its orange inner glow leaking forward around both sides of the post in two thin rose-gold arcs across the moss.

An ember-moss pot lying on its side with the open end facing the surface, the orange glow rolling out in a low fan that turns three pebbles on the stone to molten copper and warms the moss between them to deep gold, the lid used as a wedge.

A beeswax stub set inside a curl of cork-bark propped with its opening facing away from her and toward the surface, the backscatter off the pale cork catching the near row of upright cords in warm apricot while her eyes stay in cool indigo shadow.

A hollowed rose-hip swung on a milkweed-floss thread from a low twig and held against the trunk behind her, its red skin making everything it touches ember-orange: one trailing wing-tip, the outside of her elbow, the pebble nearest it glowing like a coal.

A candle in a snail shell set into a split in the bark directly behind the work-pad, the shell's mouth aimed forward, the flame's gold leaking out only through the shell's aperture in a cone that covers the front pebble row and one side of her thumb.

A twist of luminous reed-fungus pressed under a flat stone lifted at one edge by a wedge of twig so the glow escapes in a horizontal slit, washing the near surface in warm teal-gold and turning a loose bead rolling toward the edge to bright amber.

A fat glow-worm laid in a hollow of wet moss with a curl of birch bark propped in front, throwing apricot upward along the row of upright grass cords while a snail inches steadily across the whole night's work.

A firefly shut in a walnut shell, the shell tipped on its side so the opening aims at the surface and amber light pools along the near rim, warming one set of cold knuckles gold while a loose bead rocks gently at the edge.

A bead of amber pressed between two fingers and breathed on until it shines from inside, the fist half-closed so only the gap at the thumb leaks rose-gold across one cheek and the underside of a folded wing-edge.

A stub of beeswax in a curl of bark set down behind the work, the flame on the far side so only a narrow ember-orange stripe crosses the nearest row of beads on their grass cords and the backs of two reaching fingers.

Three glow-worms folded into a leaf packet held under the chin, the leaf pressed almost shut so their joined light comes out teal-edged and gold-centred across the underside of the jaw and one pale wrist reaching forward.

A hollowed rose-hip with a floss wick, set into a crack in the surface below eye level, its red skin turning everything close to it ember-orange — one ear, a cluster of pin-heads pushed into moss, and a moth asleep nearby with its wings still spread.

A candle in a snail shell sunk into a rain-pool hollow so the flame sits below the surface, throwing warm gold upward and doubling itself in the still water while one grass cord trails its end into the reflection.

A dish of oil burning a single low flame, a broad dock leaf bent over it as a hood so the glow comes only forward in a gold wedge across the row of pebbles laid on stone and the tip of one outstretched toe.

An ember in a nutshell being blown on, flaring apricot for two seconds across the whole pad of moss and the pins standing in it, the fae leaning far forward so her nose nearly touches it and one wing-tip catches the sudden rise of warmth.
A bracket fungus on the bark behind her glowing honey-amber on its own, putting a long warm rim down her spine and the trailing edge of one wing while the front of her stays cool as the sky.

A little clay pot of ember-moss with its lid slid three-quarters across, set low so the slit of gold light falls upward along a column of beads on their upright cord and gilds the underside of each bead rose-copper.

A hot river pebble lifted from the fire and wrapped in green leaves, glowing ember-orange at every seam, tucked behind the work so its leaking warmth puts a soft apricot line along the nearest grass cord and one reaching forearm.

A handful of luminous seeds tipped into a cupped bark dish and covered with a second piece of bark slid almost shut, the slit of gold light falling precisely across the wet moss where the pins stand and making the pin-heads shine like tiny suns.

A firefly trapped under a half-acorn cap, the open end tipped to face the surface, throwing a tight circle of apricot onto the pebble row and making one displaced pebble — rolled too far — glow like a small planet on its own.

A glow-worm on a twig laid across a hollow in the bark, a rolled leaf above it as a tunnel so the light travels only forward in a warm green-gold stripe across the tips of the upright cords and the knots between them.

A rose-hip lantern with its wick leaning sideways, the red skin turning the near rim of the moss pad deep ember-orange, while a grain of dew caught on a pin-head takes the colour and holds it like a garnet.

An ember carried in a folded acorn cap, the fae running back toward the work with it cupped in both hands, the gaps between her fingers striping her own wrists gold and apricot in quick bars as she moves.

A beeswax stub in a mussel-shell cradle set behind the tallest beaded cord so the cord itself becomes a silhouette and only its beads, edge-lit, each burn a warm copper rim against the cool of the cord.

Three glow-worms in a folded leaf packet set down in a hollow and squeezed half-shut, their teal-and-amber glow coming up from below the surface to light the undersides of the overhanging beads and one dangling grass fringe from beneath.

A warmed amber bead pressed into a crack in the working surface, glowing from inside, turning the grain of the bark around it rich gold and warming the nearest row of knotted grass cord to the colour of honey while a beetle stands beside it, recruited to hold a thread end flat.

A candle in a snail shell propped on its lip so the flame leans away from her eyes, throwing a long warm streak of gold along the line of pins in the moss and making one wing-edge, caught at the wrong angle, flare apricot.

A firefly shut in a walnut shell with a red petal stuffed in the opening, the light filtering through the petal to come out rose-magenta across one shoulder, a row of seed-beads, and the backs of two cold reaching fingers.

A pot of ember-moss sunk to its rim in the surface, lid slid half across and turned so the opening faces away from her, its glow bouncing off the bark behind and returning as diffuse apricot that warms the near side of every upright cord.

A hot stone wrapped in birch leaves set behind the whole work, glowing amber at its leaf-seams, making a soft warm halo that catches only the raised parts — pin-heads, bead-tops, the highest knot on the cord — and leaves the hollows cool violet.

A hollowed acorn with a moss wick soaked in pine resin, set down low so the flame is below the level of the working surface and only its upward glow reaches her — warming the underside of her chin and the lowest row of beads to a deep apricot, a dewdrop on the nearest bead gone milky with cold.

A glow-worm on a twig tucked behind a propped piece of cork bark, the cork acting as a shield so only the light that spills over its top edge reaches her, a soft gold shelf falling across the top row of pebbles and the wrist resting on them.

A luminous seed tied to the tallest grass cord so it hangs at mid-height, the cord twisting slowly and swinging the gold point of light in a small arc that crosses the beads below it with a warm stripe and then releases them back to the cool of the sky.

A clay ember-pot with its lid slid to one side just enough, set at the base of the work behind a fold of bark, the slit of ember-orange light coming through low and making the row of laid pebbles cast tiny warm shadows toward her — one pebble standing upright by accident casting a shadow twice its own height.

An oil dish with a single low flame sunk into a hollow so its rim is level with the surface, a half-acorn propped as a windbreak on the near side, throwing the warmth away from her face and across the far row of beads, each one taking the colour differently — rose, copper, gold — depending on its height.

A bead of amber held under a cupped palm and breathed on in short bursts, flaring and fading, and in the moment of its brightest pulse it warms the whole pad of moss to gold, makes the pin-heads into tiny sparks, and lights the underside of the fae's nose and both cheekbones apricot before she cups her hand shut and the sky comes back.

A fat glow-worm laid in a hollow scooped into the moss-pad, the rim of the hollow blocking it forward, so only the upright grass cords catch it from below in warm gold — a single seed has rolled into the hollow and sits there glowing too.

A candle stub in a snail shell set down behind the work, its flame toward the trunk, throwing an apricot rim along her shoulder blade and one folded wing-edge — a moth has landed on the shell and stands there warming its feet.

A bead of amber pressed between two fingers and breathed on until the heat wakes its inner honey-glow, held below the surface so it lights the underside of her chin and the curve of cold fingers rose-warm — one finger has gone briefly transparent.

A hollowed rose-hip with a milkweed-floss wick, set behind a curl of bark so the red-filtered glow falls only on the near row of pins and the wet moss around them, turning them ember-orange — the bark shield has a beetle clinging to its back.

A dish of oil with a single low wick sunk into a rain-pool hollow in the bark, the pool's walls shading it on three sides, its gold reflection lighting the undersides of the upright cords from below — a dewdrop at the rim has gone a perfect molten apricot.

Three glow-worms in a folded leaf packet held under the surface and tilted so the green-gold seeps up between the grass cords like light through a floor — a spare pebble balanced on the packet keeps it from tipping.

An ember carried in a nutshell and blown on to brighten it, held in a cupped palm with fingers pressed together, the glow leaking between knuckles in thin rose-orange lines and washing the near row of beads amber — one knuckle has gone translucently pink.

A stub of beeswax in a curl of birch bark propped as a shield on the far side of the moss-pad, the flame hidden behind it so only a gold stripe crosses the tops of the tallest pins and the wet lichen edge — the curl is slowly unrolling toward the flame.

A bracket fungus on the trunk just behind the work surface, glowing honey-warm entirely on its own, putting a long apricot sweep down one wing-edge and the back of her hand without touching her face — a snail is crossing it very slowly from left to right.

A little pot of ember-moss with its lid slid three-quarters shut, tucked into a crack below the surface so only a warm orange slot of light escapes upward and gilds the bottoms of the hanging bead-cords — one bead has swung into the slot and glows like a small sun.

A firefly shut in a walnut shell, a dock leaf bent over it as a hood and held in place by a thorn, so only a wan gold ribbon escapes sideways and runs along the ridge of the moss and across two pebbles in the count-row — the firefly is still flashing, and the ribbon pulses.

A hot river pebble lifted from a banked coal and wrapped in green leaves, its heat glowing at every split seam in deep ember-orange, set behind the work and low so the seams stripe the backs of her wrist and the nearest upright cord — a water droplet on the pebble is hissing quietly to steam.

A handful of luminous seeds cupped in both palms with thumbs crossed, the gold leaking between thumb and forefinger to fall on the cord she is threading and the bead sitting at the knot, turning the bead a warm topaz — she has tipped her hands too far and one seed is rolling.

A pine-resin bead threaded on a grass stem and warmed between the lips until it lights from inside, then clipped by its stem into a crack behind the surface so the amber glow falls across the moss in one low round pool — the stem is bent at a sharp angle from being bitten.

A candle in a second snail shell set inside the first larger shell as a chimney, so the flame is entirely enclosed and only a ring of warm gold escapes the lip, landing on the curve of her forearm and the pebbles beside it — the outer shell has a crack and a rose line runs up her sleeve.
